children: The upcoming Motorola flagship is expected to have a 200MP primary shooter and a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro chipset

Motorola looks set to take the curtains off its second-generation Signature flagship, the Signature 27, with the device positioned as a direct rival to the Galaxy S26 Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Unusually for a device this significant, the brand has kept its own teaser campaign brief, with only a handful of confirmed details trickling out via social media in the run-up to the reveal.

The headline upgrade is the primary rear camera, confirmed at 200 megapixels, a considerable jump from the 50MP main sensor on the original Signature, which was itself well regarded for its photography and videography. Reports suggest the new sensor is Sony's Lytia 901, also found on the Vivo X300 Ultra, hinting that Motorola is chasing imaging parity with Samsung's current flagship, and potentially the iPhone 18 Pro Max and Pixel 11 Pro XL as well.

Motorola has confirmed two colourways for the Signature 27: Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Olive, with speculation that additional finishes could be revealed on the day. The brand also appears to be moving toward a vegan leather back, a departure from the "linen-inspired" and "twill-inspired" glass finishes seen on the first-generation model, and a nod to materials the company has favoured in the past.
Chipset: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro Likely

Early indications point to a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro under the hood, a chip that had not been formally introduced by Qualcomm at the time of writing, with the Snapdragon Summit taking place around the same window. The original Signature ran a non-Elite Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, so this would represent a meaningful jump in raw performance for the series.

The device is officially slated for a 22 September reveal, though a wider commercial rollout, potentially stretching into India, Brazil and Europe, may come later in the year. Notably, Motorola's regional promotion has so far been concentrated on its Brazil and India social channels, with the United States conspicuously quiet, raising questions over whether, or when, the Signature 27 will reach American shelves.
